item.title: Nets Crumble Without Porter Jr. As Grizzlies Dominate
item.description: Matthew Smith-Imagn Images The Brooklyn Nets fell apart after their top scorer was ruled out before tipoff for personal reasons. They lost 129-110 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night at FedEx Forum before a crowd of 15,103 fans. Michael Porter Jr. was Brooklyn’s leading scorer, but he played in his uniform, not street clothes. Brooklyn coach Jordi Fernández explained the late timing of the news. He said, “No, not yet. A personal situation came up as we were coming to the arena. So that’s why it was announced late.” Fernández added that the team still lacks details on when Porter might return. “We don’t have any more information right now,” he told the press. Porter was listed as questionable earlier in the day before the team ruled him out an hour before tipoff. Cam Spencer sank a three-pointer to push the score to 35-17 with only 2:47 remaining in the first quarter. The Grizzlies built a massive lead that Brooklyn could not close even when Julius Randle hit a shot. Despite securing a team-leading 22 points and five assists, Randle had trouble on the glass, managing only four rebounds. He was also a minus-18, showing how much the team struggled without their main scoring option. Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double. He recorded 16 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists in the losing effort. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. also returned to action after missing time due to illness. He played 19 minutes but could not change the outcome of the game. Memphis controlled the pace without their own leading scorer, Ty Jerome. Cedrick Coward scored a game-high 23 points for the Grizzlies. Taylor Hendricks added 22 points and helped seal the victory with a dunk that put Memphis up 101-78 late in the third quarter. The Nets gave up a 16-1 run. The team fell behind by 26 points after a three-pointer by Javon Small with 7:08 left to play. Porter leads the Nets in scoring with 21.5 points per game this season. He has been a key part of the offense alongside Randle, helping the team run more efficient plays. The team had shifted away from too many isolation plays to use more dynamic offense with Porter and Sharpe. The loss marks a rough end to a four-game road trip for the Brooklyn franchise.

item.title: Man United in race to sign Koni De Winter, Milan’s stance is clear
item.description: Man United in race to sign Koni De Winter, Milan’s stance is clear Mauricio Pochettino is expected to target a central defender in his first transfer window as Manchester United’s manager. Earlier today, we relayed a report from The Telegraph suggesting Pochettino will want to strengthen United’s defence “as a matter of urgency.” United are likely to prefer a Premier League-proven defender, but the cost of signing a player from an English club mid-season may prove to be massive for the Red Devils. Interest in Koni De Winter intensifying Ruben Amorim is currently in charge of AC Milan, having joined the Serie A powerhouses after being sacked from Manchester United. The Portuguese head coach is thought to be keen on strengthening Milan’s defence. According to Tuttomercatoweb , Milan will sign a top-tier defender in January, but at the same time, there are some question marks over the future of their promising centre-back Koni De Winter . It is claimed there are new developments regarding De Winter, who has been described as one of Amorim’s most loyal supporters in Milan. De Winter is enjoying a phenomenal season under Amorim, impressing with his imposing presence and mobility at the back. As such, the Rossoneri’s intention is to keep hold of him. However, it is believed the Belgian’s performances have not gone unnoticed, especially in the Premier League. The report states that in recent days, De Winter has caught the attention of some high-profile clubs. K. De Winter – 2026/27 Page 1 of 3 1 2 3 Manchester United show interest in Koni De Winter It is understood Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool have made no secret of their interest in the Belgian international. As things stand, nothing is thought to be concrete, but the 24-year-old is highly regarded. Milan would reportedly not change their stance unless they receive offers well above his market value. De Winter is tied to Milan until 2030, having joined the Serie A giants from Genoa in 2025. As such, this pursuit could prove to be tricky for the Red Devils. Noussair Mazraoui has been strongly linked with Milan since Amorim moved to San Siro, and perhaps United could be tempted to use the Moroccan to land De Winter at a more desired fee. item.title: No. 1 South Carolina holds off JuJu Watkins’ No. 3 USC
item.description: GREENVILLE, S.C. — Not six minutes into an event dubbed “The Real SC” — after all, why go with something as simple as “No. 1 South Carolina versus No. 3 USC” when you can pretend the stakes are existential — things got real feisty. The ball found its way into the hands of Gamecocks forward Chloe Kitts. JuJu Watkins swarmed for the Trojans. Watkins and Kitts yanked and fought past the whistle for a jump ball. The USC star then brushed by Kitts as she walked away, spiking the volume in Bon Secours Arena, which included her front-row fan club featuring Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. One mid-November game won’t define the teams in it, but it can say something about the order of priority from there. Sunday was an opportunity for USC, in pursuit of its first national title in more than 40 years, to venture into hostility and assert itself in that territory. But an 89-85 win for the Gamecocks was, in the end, a product of players who have been there and done that doing it once again. The veteran trio of Tessa Johnson, Joyce Edwards and Kitts combined for 63 points and junior Jordan Lee hustled back for a block on a shot from Watkins that could’ve tied the game with 15.6 seconds left. USC’s stars struggled with efficiency for the better part of the afternoon, with sophomore Jazzy Davidson and freshman Saniyah Hall in particular showing their youth in moments. Then they demonstrated how dangerous they can be at the very end, nearly overcoming an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. Watkins, a national player of the year favorite, scored 11 of her 25 points in the final frame. This story will be updated. This article originally appeared in The Athletic . item.title: Weather is usually great at Charles Schwab but these 2 elements present a challenge
item.description: PHOENIX — Like pro golf in other places this time of year, shorter days and earlier sunsets add a little something to the mix. At the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, long shadows late in the day throw shade on many of the holes on the second nine at Phoenix Country Club. The field is just 36 qualifiers for this PGA Tour Champions season finale but the first tee time isn't until 10:25 a.m. local, with the final pairing heading out at 1:05 p.m. local. Sunset this time of year is right around 5:30 p.m., and with the senior golfers, who play in twosomes, usually moving at a pretty good clip, it's not a matter of running out of daylight. But the tall trees on the property cast some long shadows on the narrow corridors and greens late in the day on this parkland-style layout. Those shadows appear to be quite pronounced on TV during Golf Channel's coverage but for the players, it's just another thing they deal with. "It doesn't really affect it that much because it's not like you're, I mean, we've played here. With the exception of Zach [Johnson, a first-timer in this event], most have played here some," said first-round leader Stewart Cink, who had eight straight pars on Nos. 8 through 15 before closing with birdies on 16 and 18. "You kind of know what the ball's going to do on the greens. You're not just like learning for the first time in the shadows." Another element, at least on the par-4 12th and the par-4 14th, is the late-afternoon ball of fire in the sky. "I thought the difficult part was a lot of these holes just go directly into the setting sun and as the afternoon wore on, there was a lot of shots where you had a hard time picking out the flag because the sun was sinking low," Cink said. "Everybody has to deal with that a little bit, it's not a big factor, but it definitely was something noticeable." Todd Kelly is Golfweek's assistant managing editor . item.title: Michael Kim explains why Rory McIlroy had a ‘big advantage’ over Eugenio Chacarra in Race to Dubai battle
item.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images Rory McIlroy produced a late comeback to overtake Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai standings on the final day of the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy’s solo second-place finish was enough to secure the season-long title, despite Chacarra also enjoying an impressive week with a tied-third finish. Tyrrell Hatton claimed victory in Dubai, but the biggest prize went to McIlroy, who has now won a record-equalling eight Race to Dubai titles alongside Colin Montgomerie. PGA Tour player Michael Kim has since explained why the Northern Irishman held a significant advantage over Chacarra throughout the season. Michael Kim reveals Rory McIlroy’s key advantage over Eugenio Chacarra Michael Kim believes Rory McIlroy had a significant advantage over Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai battle because of the way points are distributed across the DP World Tour season. He pointed to the weighting given to major championships as a key factor in the 37-year-old’s success. “Rory had a big advantage, with the points very far skewed toward the majors. Eugenio played awesome this year to even give himself a shot at the Race to Dubai,” Kim tweeted. McIlroy’s major championship performances proved crucial, as he won the Masters and finished tied seventh at the PGA Championship. He also recorded top-40 finishes at both the US Open and The Open, while Chacarra featured in just one major, finishing tied-46th at Royal Birkdale. The Spaniard enjoyed an excellent season on the DP World Tour , winning the Italian Open, Dutch Open and India Championship. He also finished tied-22nd in Abu Dhabi and third in Dubai, but those results were not enough to overhaul McIlroy. The back-to-back Masters champion finished third in Abu Dhabi and second in Dubai to claim his eighth Race to Dubai title. Chacarra may have missed out on the Order of Merit, but he has plenty to celebrate after securing his PGA Tour card for next season. Kim expects the former LIV Golfer to make an immediate impact in the United States, particularly given how much time he already spends there. He believes the transition will be straightforward and has tipped Chacarra to become a major presence on the PGA Tour. Kim continued: “He already spends most of his time in America, so it’s going to be an easy transition for him. He’s going to be a force on the PGA Tour next year. item.title: U.S. women's hockey team gets Canada in world championship final with historic streak at stake
item.description: The U.S. and Canada will meet in the World Women's Hockey Championship final for the 24th time in 25 all-time editions. This time, the U.S. is carrying its longest winning streak in major international competition. The reigning Olympic and world champion beat Finland 5-0 in the semifinals on Sunday in Denmark. Later, Canada won 3-0 over Sweden, which made its first world semi since 2009. The Americans are 6-0 at these worlds, winning every game by at least five goals. Since the start of the 2025 Worlds, the U.S. has won 20 consecutive games between World Championship and Olympic play, a program record. On Sunday, captain Hilary Knight led the way with one goal and one assist, while Aerin Frankel stopped all 13 Finland shots. Earlier in the tournament, the U.S. broke the record for most shots in a single women's worlds game, registering 85 in a 14-0 quarterfinal win over Denmark on Friday. The U.S. had the previous record of 82 from 1997. The 14 goals marked the most for the U.S. in a worlds game since 2000. Frankel broke the American goalie record for most career game wins in worlds history. Frankel is now up to 20 victories, bettering Jessie Vetter's old record of 16. Caroline Harvey broke the record for most career points in world championship play for a U.S. defender, even though she is still just 24 years old. Knight, playing in her 16th worlds at age 37, leads the tournament with seven goals in six games, while Harvey has the most points (15) and Taylor Fox (née Heise) has the most assists (12). Canada is playing a major tournament without Marie-Philip Poulin for the first time since 2008. Poulin had surgery in July for a torn ACL and meniscus. item.title: Draymond Green on what was behind poor Jaylen Brown outing vs. Boston Celtics
item.description: While fans of the Boston Celtics may not always love what Golden State Warriors vet big man Draymond Green does on the court, he also tends to be as even-keeled in his takes off the court as his play most definitely is not on it. On a recent episode of his eponymous podcast, the Michigan State alum had praise for the Celtics after their win over the Philadelphia 76ers last week – as well as a critique of how former Celtics forward Jaylen Brown handled his first contest against his former team that may resonate with some Boston fans after what transpired before and after the tilt. "I think a lot of people thought Boston (was) about to fall off," offered Green. "(That Paul George) doesn't have it anymore. And Boston has picked right up where they left off at. PG is looking really good. (Jayson Tatum) is starting to look like JT again. They're shooting the ball well; they're playing their brand of basketball. They look good. They look really good." Then, the Dubs vet shifted his focus to what went wrong for Brown and the 76ers. "JT tried to dap Jaylen Brown up prior to the tip off," said Green. "Jaylen Brown ignored him. I didn't really love that, and I didn't love it because feel how you want to feel (...)." "I've got a ton of respect for Jaylen Brown. But I always say when things like that happen and you're not willing to speak, that says more about you than it says about the other person," said the Golden State forward. "So Jaylen Brown not saying, not making eye contact with JT, JT comes, hits you on your chest, tries to say what's up, you don't make eye contact. I think that's part of the reason Jaylen Brown played bad. Because your aura ain't right, your juju ain't right. You've got your head down and then it carried over into the game. And so I don't really love that, man. Number one, like you know, I know he's upset that he got traded, and feels like JT could have stopped it or regardless, man. I've never really got off into that when guys do that when they get traded and take it out on a player. You speak to every player, but not him. I don't really love that." "The bar is so high on the respect level for Jaylen Brown from everybody, and he's earned that respect. Just to see to see him do that, I don't love," closed Green. item.title: Week 11 Report Card: Exemplary grades for Oregon after Michigan win
item.description: When the Oregon Ducks came in at No. 16 in the College Football Playoff rankings this week, the possibility of earning an at-large bid to the 12-team field appeared to be on the table. While the three losses that the Ducks have on their resume isn't ideal, they've played like a playoff team the two previous weeks. That needed to continue in the final three regular season games for the Playoff Committee to even be able to consider placing Oregon in the CFP. Game one of three, coming against the Michigan Wolverines , check. Oregon looked about as impressive as they could've hoped on Saturday, putting the locks on Michigan's offense in allowing just a single touchdown in the 31-7 convincing win. The 31 points (four touchdowns, one field goal) was the most that the Wolverines have allowed all season long — by a whopping ten points. At times, the Ducks looked like a far more physical team than the Wolverines, widely-regarded for their physicality and toughness. If the Playoff Committee isn't impressed with a win in which nearly every positon group for the Ducks excelled, I'm not sure what else they could do. Let's get into this week's report card, where it's difficult to find much criticism and easy to find a lot of praise after the 23-point victory. Quarterbacks Grade: A There was only one definite throw that Dylan Raiola made in which he put the ball in serious harms way. But other than that, Raiola was nails and put forth his best performance as the Ducks' starter this season. He was precise and on fire from the very beginning, finishing the first quarter going 8-for-8 for 133 yards and two touchdowns, one being a 60-yard moon ball to Jeremiah McClellan. The next drive, he floated a pass to Evan Stewart for another big gain. Raiola has been on the field a lot in 2026, and this was the best version. Running Backs Grade: A- With Jordon Davison still out injured, it was up to Dierre Hill Jr. to take a bulk of the carries out of the backfield. In toting the rock 21 times, Hill churned out 98 yards including a long of 36 yards. Each of Hill's best skills were on display, as he was dynamic with the football on each touch. He caught a swing pass in the fourth quarter and weaved his way for a 49-yard touchdown, putting the Wolverines out of their misery. True freshman Brandon Smith also recorded 29 rushing yards on seven carries while Da'Jaun Riggs caught a short touchdown out of the backfield. Wide Receivers/Tight Ends Grade: A- The headliner of this unit was Jeremiah McClellan, who surpassed 100 receiving yards in his second game back from a broken foot. His 60-yard touchdown on the opening drive affirmed that he was back to full strength, as he ran past multiple Wolverines despite being held. Dakorien Moore was his usual reliable self, catching seven passes for 88 yards and a score — though he did drop a would-be touchdown in the end zone, leading to the A- grade. item.title: Alyssa Klebasko’s save sends No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey to the NCAA Tournament semifinals with a 2-1 win over Duke
item.description: As time ticked down in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s NCAA quarterfinal match, No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey clung to a one-goal lead against former ACC rival Duke. After a video review, Duke was awarded a penalty stroke with 1:16 left. Midfielder Julia Boehringer lined up against Alyssa Klebasko with the crowd on the edge of its seat and players locked arm in arm. Boehringer chose to go to Klebasko’s right, but so did Klebasko. The Big Ten Goalkeeper of the Year made a career-defining save, knocking down Boehringer’s shot with her blocker to clinch the 2-1 victory and Maryland’s spot at championship weekend. “Honestly, I was just staying present, and we do strokes almost every day in practice, so I knew that I could save it,” Klebasko said. “Also, we pulled that girl’s old strokes, and I watched each stroke about ten times last night – her footwork, where she placed her hands – so as soon as I saw her step, I knew she was going upper-right, and I was able to step that way.” The first quarter went by without any scoring. Maryland had chances to break the deadlock throughout the opening period, but Duke’s defense was up to the task. The Blue Devils goalkeeper Kaiya Chepow picked up a big-time stop on an early shot by Maryland’s Maci Bradford while the rest of Duke’s defense denied the Terps on a pair of penalty corners. On the other side, Maryland’s defense prevented Duke from sustaining attacks. The Terps were aggressive in the midfield, forcing loose balls and intercepting plenty of passes. The Blue Devils tried just one shot in the period, which sailed wide. The Terps nearly cracked the code to start the second, but Ella Beach’s shot clanked off the post. Eight minutes later, the pressure paid off. Jordyn Hollamon displayed her agility, zig-zagging through countless defenders with fancy stickwork before driving a shot past Chepow. The goal — Hollamon’s 10th of the season — elicited an eruption from the Maryland side as the Terps took the 1-0 lead. Maryland had a golden chance to double the advantage late in the second frame with four consecutive corners, but Duke held strong. Boehringer made a massive defensive save on a shot from Francisca Eschoyez, and Sophia Miller broke up a pass to the far post to keep the Terps at bay. Duke couldn’t muster any offense in the second quarter. The Blue Devils neither took a shot nor forced a corner in the second period, and they entered halftime scoreless. Maryland hampered Duke’s attack throughout the first 30 minutes. As the Blue Devils approached the shooting circle, the Terps compacted, swarming the player with the ball and making it difficult for her to shoot or pass. Duke continuously argued for penalty corners to no avail. The third quarter was a frame of firsts for Duke, as the Blue Devils forced their first corner, took their first shot on goal and scored their first tally. item.title: On Keeping Crosby, Malkin Together: ‘The Option’s There’
item.description: Pittsburgh Penguins coach Dan Muse had the perfect opening to make tweaks – or even tsunamis – to his personnel on Sunday. The team doesn’t play again until Thursday and was coming off a frustrating 4-1 loss to Ottawa. Instead, Muse held course, with the lines , defensive pairs and power-play units the same during practice at the UPMC Lemieux Sports Complex. That meant that the top line still sported Evgeni Malkin , Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell . Long-time teammates and future Hall of Famers Malkin, 40, and Crosby, 39, have played together at times over the years. Early on, sometimes they would last on the same line for a few games. In recent years, it’s been more of a situational thing – thrown together after a penalty kill or for a few shifts to try to spark some offense. But it’s been four games now with that top line. The return of injured winger Bryan Rust could provide a reason to break up that trio, but his return is not imminent – he and forward Elmer Soderblom continue to skate before practice. So could Crosby and Malkin remain together for a while this time? “Yeah, I think so,” Penguins coach Dan Muse said. “Every year’s different. With that and everything else, sometimes you make changes over the course of the year. It’s something that we wanted to see. I know that they do have time together in the past, so there’s some familiarity there. I think the option’s there for sure.” Of course, with the way the lines have been shuffled as the Penguins seek consistency and balance, the coaches could just as well break up that line by practice Monday. One facilitating factor for keeping it intact is Malkin’s move from center to wing last season. Previously, placing him on Crosby’s line diluted the team’s strength down the middle, and so was nearly always considered a temporary solution to a sagging offense. It could also be pointed out that with those two veterans – three if you include Rakell – together, it potentially opens up more room for younger players on the other lines. So in a season that seems to be stuck in the mud , why not keep them together for the foreseeable future? The guy who makes up the third portion of the line, Rakell, is convinced it could work. “Yeah, I think so. We’re very familiar with everybody’s game and tendencies on the ice,” he said. “Just trying to work off each other. We can make things happen off the rush. But also when we’re all going, we’re very comfortable being on the forecheck and scoring on rebounds. “I think we can get better and better, and try to lead the way for the team.” In their four games since the line was formed, Crosby has a two goals and an assist, Malkin has six assists, and Rakell has a goal and an assist. While they had no points and seemed quiet in the game Saturday against Ottawa, their metrics as a line combination are good, including a 75.00 GF%, 71.43 HDCF% and 62.10 Corsi For. Muse smiled when asked about their advanced stats and the impact that might have on keeping them together.

item.title: Louisville embarrassed at Memphis, 98-78
item.description: FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 28: Head Coach Penny Hardaway of the Memphis Tigers signals to the bench during a game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Bud Walton Arena on October 28, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. The Razorbacks defeated the Tigers 93-81. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images For a season that was supposed to be different in all the right ways, Sunday felt an awful lot like the same song and dance Louisville fans have seen from previous Pat Kelsey teams in big spots on the road. U of L led by as many as 18 points in the first half and by 11 at halftime, but was destroyed in the second half by unranked Memphis, who rolled to a 98-78 victory over their longtime rivals to the North. The comeback was the fourth-largest in the last 15 years by an unranked team against an AP top 10 opponent. The Tigers shot over 70 percent from the field in the second half and out-scored their visitors 57-26 after the break. Point guard Jayden Reid led the way with 24 points and 10 assists, while Tylik Weeks added 24 points of his own, 18 of those coming in the second half. Seth Trimble seemed to be the only Cardinal not rattled during the second half avalanche. The transfer from North Carolina scored 16 points and added two steals and two blocks. Jackson Shelstad scored 16 as well, but had just one made basket after halftime. Look, there’s no way to sugarcoat it: This was a very very, VERY bad way to, in earnest, begin what we all agree is pretty much a defining season for Pat Kelsey at Louisville. In a major spot, the Cards were once again the less composed, less tough, and less hungry team. That can’t happen when we’re talking about one of the 5-10 highest-paid rosters in the sport and a team that many experts believe should be a Final Four contender. You went all in last spring on being one of the best defensive teams in the country, and you just gave up 98 to a Memphis team playing without its second-leading scorer. This team needs to be elite defensively to have any shot whatsoever at being great overall. Sunday, it wasn’t even average defensively. I know it’s November, but these three games coming up in Las Vegas on Thanksgiving Week could not be more important.

item.title: Boston College Overcomes Poor Shooting, Defeats UNH 67-55
item.description: On Sunday afternoon, Boston College defeated UNH 67-55 to improve to 4-0 on the young season. New Hampshire jumped out to a quick 13-2 lead over the first 4:50 of the game, with BC’s early-season shooting struggles continuing. The Eagles—missing star guard Money Williams, who per ESPN’s Jeff Borzello is game-to-game—missed seven of their first eight shots. A couple threes from Ernest Shelton kept the Eagles afloat, who also welcomed back UConn transfer Jacob Furphy for his first appearance in an Eagles jersey. By the 10-minute mark, the Eagles had trimmed the deficit to one; a Zak Smrekar and-one layup at 8:12 gave BC their first lead. Furphy drilled a wing three for his first points in an Eagle uniform, and Smrekar cleaned up a Furphy missed layup on the next possession as BC’s offense found a bit of a rhythm. UNH, however, continued to stay hot from beyond the arc to stay within reach. The Wildcats hit four of their first nine treys, fueling their offense. BC’s Ernest Shelton—billed as a sniper after an offseason transfer from Merrimack despite early-season inconsistency—continued his hot half with back-to-back triples late in the half to put BC up 31-28 at half (despite shooting a putrid 33% from the floor). The second half began much as the first half ended: with both teams trading buckets. Luke Hunger connected from close range to briefly push BC’s lead to five, but UNH answered with an immediate lay of their own. A quick 9-0 run five minutes into the second half, sparked by Shelton’s fifth three and a Smrekar bucket, helped the Eagles pad their lead to double-digits. BC’s offense, while far from perfect, was able to generate enough clean looks to keep UNH at bay. The amount of misses, however, was definitely concerning; Zak Smrekar and Jacob Furphy combined to shoot for 9-27 today. Despite the poor shooting, BC’s defense, ability to manufacture extra possessions, and timely rebounding afforded BC a roughly 10-point lead for the last quarter of the game. Smrekar connected on his first trey with 2:43 left in the game to put BC up 13, and BC went on to seal the 67-55 win.

(Photo by Norm Hall/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) With the 2026 Arizona Fall League in the books, let’s take a look at how each Brewers prospect fared with the Scottsdale Scorpions. Jett Williams Williams, who’s getting his feet back under him after missing the last three months of the season with a right wrist injury, hit just .217 (15-for-69), but five of those 15 hits went for extra bases (a home run, two doubles, and two triples).
